description:
“戏剧是什么？”这是戏剧导演赵易阳反复思考、并尝试回答的问题。
在他看来， 戏剧不仅是一种表演艺术，更像是一把隐形的椅子，让那些无处安放的情绪坐下来，得以被看见。
在这场演讲中，他以简单而真实的故事切入，从木河马的孤独到小山村的戏剧社，他让我们看到：在戏剧的世界里，没有对错，只有“尝试”；这是一种开放的拥抱，能帮助每个人看见自己，看见彼此。
戏剧就像一座桥梁，在生活的洪流中，连接孤独与共鸣，安全地接住隐藏的情绪与故事，并将之缓缓导向治愈与希望。 深圳超级猴戏剧Club创始人

description:
Have you ever wanted to post online but felt like you'd be judged? Joe Gannon, founder of a social media agency, explains why the people with the most valuable experience are often the ones who stay silent and what it's costing them.

In this TEDx talk, Joe introduces the concept of "visibility debt", the widening gap between who you are and what the world sees when fear keeps you from sharing your ideas. Drawing on Jakob Nielsen's 90-9-1 rule (90% of people never post, 9% post occasionally, and just 1% create most of the content we consume), Joe explains why public speaking is our #1 human fear, why your biggest insecurity might be your greatest strength, and how preparation, not luck, is what turns a high-stakes moment into a life-changing opportunity. Joe Gannon is a personal brand strategist, founder of Amplify and creator of Personal Brand Mastery. He has spent over seven years helping entrepreneurs, founders and thought leaders turn their ideas into influence, with Amplify suppo
title: The Hidden Cost Of Not Posting Online | Joe Gannon | TEDxBlack Mountain

author: TEDx Talks
description:
國岡　啓子　：　「価値あるもの」が「評価されるもの」になるまでの物語

25年以上、在野の研究者として、子育てや家事をしながら、途方もない量のデータベースを作成してきた彼女。
がんばって作っても、このデータベースは世に出ることはないかもしれない。
いっそやめてしまおうと諦めそうになったこともあった。
そんな彼女が辿り着いた、「価値あるもの」と「評価されるもの」との間にあるものとは。

KUNIOKA Keiko　：　The Journey from What Has Value to What Is Valued

For more than 25 years, she has worked as an independent researcher,
building an enormous database while raising children and managing household responsibilities.
No matter how hard she worked on it, there were times when she feared that this database might never see the light of day.
At times, she came close to giving up altogether.
What she eventually discovered was the crucial element that lies between something of value and something that is truly valued.


 After graduating from university, she studied bureaucratic personnel affairs in the Meiji era as a researcher out of power for a long time. The results of her  research are now being distributed by her university as a blue book DB and Kainin Nichiroku DB. Kainin Nichirok
title: 「価値あるもの」が「評価されるもの」になるまでの物語 | Keiko KUNIOKA | TEDxKumamoto

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In his talk, Eric challenges one of the most common modern beliefs: the idea that we do not need help. Starting from a simple comment left on his social media, he shows how everyday life depends on invisible systems, shared knowledge, and the contributions of countless other people. What looks like independence, he argues, is often built on unseen interdependence.

He then reframes familiar ideas such as money, work, leadership, and education through a different lens. In his view, money is stored help, jobs are exchanges of help, and careers grow as our ability to offer meaningful help grows. This shift opens a broader way of thinking about value, learning, and contribution in a fast-changing world.

Eric’s talk is ultimately a call to rethink how we relate to one another. Rather than celebrating isolation, he invites the audience to recognize that stronger families, organizations, and societies are built through mutual support, shared responsibility, and a deeper respect for the help
title: The Biggest Lie You Believe: I Don't Need Any Help | Eric McDermott | TEDxVUAmsterdam

description:
《红楼梦》是一部从未停止被讨论与解读的文学经典。然而，当代人以现代视角重新审视它时，往往容易忽略作品深处的社会背景与人性困境。
在这场演讲中，历史文化博主张志浩将目光投向《红楼梦》中“袭人”这个复杂角色，以一个小丫鬟的成长历程为起点，深挖隐藏在书本情节中的权力结构、性别文化与社会矛盾。
他通过这场分享，不仅带我们重温经典，还直面一个重要的提问：今天的我们，真的已经摆脱那些古老的困境了吗? 图书作者
文物与博物馆硕士
知名历史文化博主 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: 《红楼梦》里看不见的袭人：古今观念中权力与性别的交锋 | 志浩 张 | TEDxNanshan Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
作为一名ICU医生，余一生的工作是在危急之中为患者守住生的希望。这看似是与死神的“拔河”，其实背后是身体的自发抗争、家属艰难的抉择与人性之中巨大的心理冲突。
在这场演讲中，她带我们走进ICU，思考那些肉眼无法看见却至关重要的东西——那些来自细胞的奇迹，来自抉择的勇敢，和来自人性的温暖。
她通过16年积累的故事分享，尝试回答这样的问题：在死亡与生存的夹缝中，是什么支撑了最终的奇迹？每一次抉择的背后，都有哪些看不见却无比重要的细节？ 南京鼓楼医院重症医学科副主任医师、医疗组长
非虚构文学《只有ICU医生知道》作者 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: 看不见的生命力：ICU里的韧性与抉择 | 一生 余 | TEDxNanshan Salon
